USMLE-style practice · Pharmacology

Belching after a bicarbonate remedy

Choose the single best answer, then reveal the explanation.

A 28-year-old man takes sodium bicarbonate dissolved in water after a heavy meal. His burning discomfort briefly improves, but he begins belching within minutes. There is no diarrhea or abdominal tenderness. Which chemical product most directly explains the belching?

  1. Ammonia produced by urease inhibition
  2. Oxygen liberated by bicarbonate reduction
  3. Carbon dioxide released during acid neutralization
  4. Methane generated by immediate bacterial fermentation
  5. Hydrogen sulfide released from pepsin breakdown
Reveal answer and explanation
Correct answer

Carbon dioxide released during acid neutralization

Bicarbonate reacts with gastric acid to form water and carbon dioxide, producing gas.

Understanding the options

Carbon dioxide released during acid neutralization
Carbon dioxide is generated when bicarbonate neutralizes acid.
Methane generated by immediate bacterial fermentation
The immediate effect does not require colonic bacterial fermentation.
Hydrogen sulfide released from pepsin breakdown
Pepsin breakdown is not the relevant source of gas.
Ammonia produced by urease inhibition
Urease inhibition reduces rather than generates urease-derived ammonia.
Oxygen liberated by bicarbonate reduction
Oxygen is not a product of this acid-bicarbonate reaction.
